blocks.content: I found it at the corner of Bellamy and March.

The old hardware store has been empty for three years. Someone has been leaving flower pots on the front steps — different ones every few weeks, like a quiet argument for the place. Today there were two terracotta pots with something purple in them, and the morning light hit them at an angle I'd been looking for without knowing it.
I was setting down my bag when I heard the laugh.
I knew it before I looked up.

She was across the street with another girl — dark curls, both of them talking fast, the rhythm of two people who've been friends long enough to skip the parts in between. The dinosaur was still under her arm. She was pointing at something down the block, making a case for it. The other girl wasn't convinced. She made the case harder.
She glanced back mid-sentence — turning to point at something behind her — and for a half second she was looking at exactly the corner where I was standing.
She didn't see me. Or she did and I didn't register. There's a difference but I couldn't tell you which one it was.
They turned the corner. She was gone.
I stood there longer than made sense, holding my bag, looking at an empty street.
The flower pots were still there. The light was still good.
I set up and started painting.
